newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH FIRM TO JOIN AIRBUS SUPERJUMBO STUDY PHASE.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH FIRM TO JOIN AIRBUS SUPERJUMBO STUDY PHASE.

text.p: Finnish engineering company Finavitec said in a statement on Monday it had signed an agreement to participate in the study phase of European airplane maker Airbus' planned A3XX superjumbo aircraft.
"Participation in this phase will allow Finavitec to evaluate the extent of their future phases of the A3XX programme," it said, adding Finavitec's engineers would work in the A3XX design team.
Finavitec is 51.1 percent state-owned, 49.9 percent owned by paper machine maker Valmet , and is to become part of the state's defence materials group due for set-up this year.

The Airbus consortium comprises French Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace , Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
SAAB of Sweden had signed a similar agreement, Airbus said in a statement.
"The memoranda of understanding are expected to lead to business agreements which would represent more than two billion US dollars in business volume for SAAB and Finavitec," it said.
